chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled: “A free woman may be married over a bondwoman, but a bondwoman may not be married over a free woman.”

And whoever marries a free woman over a bondwoman must allot to the free woman twice what he allots to the bondwoman from his wealth and his person, and the bondwoman shall have one-third of his wealth and his person.

key_terms.الْأَمَةِ: a bondwoman or female slave in the context of marriage law
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: a free woman, as distinct from a bondwoman in marital rulings
key_terms.تُنْكَحَ: to be given in marriage or married
key_terms.ضِعْفَيْ: twice the amount or double share
key_terms.قَسَمَ: he apportioned or allocated fairly between wives
key_terms.مَالِهِ: his wealth, meaning financial maintenance and material support
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: his person, meaning his time and personal companionship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a free woman and a bondwoman together, and how are their rights divided?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding marriage involving a free woman and a bondwoman. It establishes the order of permissibility in such a marriage and sets out the division of the husband's financial support and personal time between them.
